questions.def: The correlative conjunction 'neither' requires 'nor' to create a negative connection.
questions.question: Neither the students ___ the teacher were prepared for the quiz.

questions.def: Inversion is required after 'Not until' at the start of a sentence.
questions.question: Not until the bell rang ___ the classroom.

questions.def: 'Deny' requires the gerund ('having stolen') and past tense agrees.
questions.question: He ___ having stolen the jewels.

questions.def: Inversion after 'Hardly' requires the auxiliary verb 'had'.
questions.question: Hardly ___ I entered the house when it started raining.

questions.def: Inversion is required after 'Little' at the start of a sentence.
questions.question: Little ___ that he was being watched.

questions.def: 'Failed' fits the context, indicating a past action.
questions.question: He ___ to submit his assignment on time.

questions.def: Inversion after 'Scarcely' requires the auxiliary verb 'had'.
questions.question: Scarcely ___ they begun the exam when the fire alarm rang.

questions.def: Inversion is required after 'Only after' at the start of a sentence.
questions.question: Only after much deliberation ___ to accept the offer.

questions.def: 'Refused' fits the context, indicating a past action.
questions.question: They ___ to comment on the matter.

questions.def: Inversion after 'Nowhere' requires the auxiliary verb 'have'.
questions.question: Nowhere ___ I seen such poverty.

questions.def: Inversion is required after 'At no time' at the start of a sentence.
questions.question: At no time ___ the safety regulations.

questions.def: 'Rejected' is the correct passive past participle form.
questions.question: The proposal was ___ by the committee.

questions.def: Inversion after 'On no account' requires the auxiliary verb 'should'.
questions.question: On no account ___ you open this document without authorization.

questions.def: Inversion is required after 'In no way' at the start of a sentence.
questions.question: In no way ___ their actions.

questions.def: 'Declined' fits the context, indicating a past action.
questions.question: They ___ our invitation to the event.

questions.def: Inversion after 'Under no circumstances' requires the auxiliary verb 'should'.
questions.question: Under no circumstances ___ this door be opened.

questions.def: Conditional type 3 uses 'would have' in the main clause.
questions.question: Were it not for his assistance, we ___.

questions.def: 'Disapproved' fits the context, indicating a past reaction.
questions.question: The manager ___ of the employee's actions.

questions.def: Inversion after 'Not for a moment' requires the auxiliary verb 'did'.
questions.question: Not for a moment ___ I believe his story.

questions.def: Inversion is required after 'Only then' at the start of a sentence.
questions.question: Only then ___ the full extent of the damage.

questions.def: 'Disagreed' fits the context, indicating a past opinion.
questions.question: They ___ with the proposed changes.

questions.def: Inversion after 'In no way' requires the auxiliary verb 'am'.
questions.question: In no way ___ I responsible for this outcome.

questions.def: Conditional type 3 uses 'would have' in the main clause.
questions.question: Had they known the truth, they ___ differently.

questions.def: Inversion after negative adverbial phrases like 'under no circumstances' requires 'should'.
questions.question: Under no circumstances ___ this document be copied.

questions.def: 'Not until' requires subject-verb inversion in the main clause.
questions.question: Not until the report was finalized ___ the team celebrate.

questions.def: 'Despite' correctly introduces a phrase indicating a denial.
questions.question: ___ having seen the file, he was dismissed.

questions.def: 'Hardly' requires inversion and the past perfect: 'Hardly had I entered'.
questions.question: Hardly ___ I entered the room when the phone rang.

questions.def: 'Nowhere' requires inversion of the auxiliary verb.
questions.question: Nowhere ___ such exquisite craftsmanship be found.

questions.def: 'Unbelievable' is the correct negation of 'believable'.
questions.question: I found his story ___.

questions.def: This is an inverted conditional; 'wouldn't' expresses the correct negation.
questions.question: Were it not for your help, I ___ have succeeded.
